tools.json-validator.faqs.0.question: How do I validate JSON?
tools.json-validator.faqs.0.answer: Paste JSON into the input field. The tool immediately checks the syntax and shows whether it's valid. If there are errors, it shows the exact location and cause.
tools.json-validator.faqs.1.question: What are common JSON errors?
tools.json-validator.faqs.1.answer: Common errors include missing commas, trailing commas, single quotes instead of double quotes, missing quotes, unclosed brackets, and invalid escape characters. The tool highlights the exact issue.
tools.json-validator.faqs.2.question: Can I validate large JSON files?
tools.json-validator.faqs.2.answer: Yes. Since validation happens in the browser, it can handle large JSON files. However, very large files (>50 MB) may be slow due to browser memory limits.
tools.json-validator.faqs.3.question: Does the validator fix JSON?
tools.json-validator.faqs.3.answer: No. The validator only checks the syntax and reports errors. You need to fix them manually. However, the error messages tell you exactly what and where to fix.
tools.json-validator.faqs.4.question: Is JSON data sent to a server?
tools.json-validator.faqs.4.answer: No. All validation happens locally in your browser. Your data never leaves your device.
tools.json-validator.faqs.5.question: Does the validator support JSON with comments (JSONC)?
tools.json-validator.faqs.5.answer: No. Standard JSON does not allow comments. If your JSON contains comments, you need to remove them before validating.

tools.loan-calculator.faqs.0.question: How is the monthly payment calculated?
tools.loan-calculator.faqs.0.answer: The calculator uses the standard amortization formula: M = P[r(1+r)^n]/[(1+r)^n-1], where P is the loan amount, r is the monthly interest rate, and n is the total number of payments.
tools.loan-calculator.faqs.1.question: What types of loans does this work for?
tools.loan-calculator.faqs.1.answer: This calculator works for any fixed-rate loan with equal monthly payments - personal loans, auto loans, student loans, home equity loans, and more. It doesn't apply to variable-rate or interest-only loans.
tools.loan-calculator.faqs.2.question: How does the loan term affect total cost?
tools.loan-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Longer terms mean lower monthly payments but significantly more total interest paid. Shorter terms have higher payments but save money overall. Always compare total cost, not just the monthly payment.

tools.mortgage-calculator.faqs.0.questio: How is the monthly mortgage payment calculated?
tools.mortgage-calculator.faqs.0.answer: The monthly payment is calculated using the standard amortization formula: M = P[r(1+r)^n]/[(1+r)^n - 1], where P is the loan amount, r is the monthly interest rate, and n is the total number of payments.
tools.mortgage-calculator.faqs.1.questio: How accurate are the property tax and insurance estimates?
tools.mortgage-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Property tax rates are based on effective rates by state. Insurance rates are based on average annual premiums by state. Both are applied as a percentage of the home price and update automatically when you change state or price. These are state averages; actual costs vary by county, city, coverage level, and property specifics.
tools.mortgage-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Private mortgage insurance (PMI) is required when your down payment is less than 20% of the home price. It typically costs 0.3%-1.5% of the loan amount per year and protects the lender in case of default.
tools.mortgage-calculator.faqs.3.questio: Why do property taxes differ so much by state?
tools.mortgage-calculator.faqs.3.answer: Property tax rates range from 0.28% in Hawaii to 2.47% in New Jersey. That means on a $350,000 home you'd pay $980 per year in Hawaii and $8,645 in New Jersey. States without income tax typically have higher property taxes to compensate.
tools.mortgage-calculator.faqs.4.questio: Why is home insurance so expensive in some states?
tools.mortgage-calculator.faqs.4.answer: Insurance costs are significantly higher in states prone to natural disasters. Florida averages about 1.05% of home value due to hurricane risk. Oklahoma and Louisiana are high due to tornado and hurricane exposure. Hawaii, Utah, and Oregon have the lowest rates.
tools.mortgage-calculator.faqs.5.questio: Does this include taxes and insurance?
tools.mortgage-calculator.faqs.5.answer: Yes. After you select a state, property taxes and home insurance are estimated automatically based on state averages and the home price. These are added to the principal and interest payment to show the true monthly cost. You can also adjust both values manually.
tools.mortgage-calculator.faqs.6.answer: An amortization schedule shows how each monthly payment is split between principal and interest over the life of the loan. Early payments are mostly interest; later payments are mostly principal.

tools.og-preview.faqs.0.answer: An Open Graph preview shows how your website looks when shared on Facebook, LinkedIn, and other social platforms. It uses your site's og: meta tags to display the title, description, image, and URL.
tools.og-preview.faqs.1.question: How do I use the OG preview?
tools.og-preview.faqs.1.answer: Enter your website URL. The tool fetches and parses the Open Graph tags, then shows previews of how it will look when shared on Facebook and Twitter.
tools.og-preview.faqs.2.question: Why does my preview look wrong?
tools.og-preview.faqs.2.answer: Check that your site has the correct og:title, og:description, og:image, and og:url tags. Images should be at least 1200x630 pixels. Some platforms cache previews, so it may take time to update.
tools.og-preview.faqs.3.question: What is the difference between Facebook and Twitter previews?
tools.og-preview.faqs.3.answer: Facebook uses Open Graph tags, while Twitter uses Twitter Card tags (falling back to Open Graph if available). The layouts and designs are also slightly different.
tools.og-preview.faqs.4.question: Can I preview the OG tags of a specific page?
tools.og-preview.faqs.4.answer: Yes. Enter any URL and the tool will fetch that page's OG tags and display the preview.
tools.og-preview.faqs.5.question: Are the previews accurate?
tools.og-preview.faqs.5.answer: Previews are based on the OG tags fetched from your website. They aim to match Facebook's and Twitter's current designs, but actual rendering may differ slightly due to platform updates.

tools.percentage-calculator.faqs.0.answe: Multiply the number by the percentage divided by 100. For example, 25% of 200 = 200 * (25/100) = 50.
tools.percentage-calculator.faqs.1.quest: How do I calculate percentage change?
tools.percentage-calculator.faqs.1.answe: Percentage change = ((new value - old value) / old value) * 100. A change from 80 to 100 is ((100-80)/80) * 100 = a 25% increase.
tools.percentage-calculator.faqs.2.quest: What's the difference between percentage and percentage points?
tools.percentage-calculator.faqs.2.answe: A change from 10% to 15% is a 5 percentage point increase, but a 50% percentage increase. Percentage points measure absolute differences; percentages measure relative change.

tools.retirement-calculator.faqs.0.answe: The 4% rule suggests you can withdraw 4% of your retirement savings per year without running out of money over 30 years. It's based on research using historical market returns. Adjust for inflation to maintain purchasing power.
tools.retirement-calculator.faqs.1.quest: How much do I need to retire?
tools.retirement-calculator.faqs.1.answe: Multiply your annual expenses by 25 (based on the 4% rule). If you need $50,000 per year, aim for $1.25 million. This includes Social Security and pensions as income sources.
tools.retirement-calculator.faqs.2.quest: How does Social Security affect retirement?
tools.retirement-calculator.faqs.2.answe: Social Security replaces about 40% of pre-retirement income. Higher earners get a lower replacement percentage. Claim at 67 (full retirement age), or wait until 70 to increase payments by 8%/year.
tools.retirement-calculator.faqs.3.answe: A rule of thumb: stock percentage = 110 - your age. At 30: 80% stocks. At 60: 50% stocks. Reduce risk as you approach retirement. But adjust based on your risk tolerance and time horizon.

tools.salary-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Divide the annual salary by the number of hours worked per year. For a standard 40-hour work week, 52 weeks: $65,000 / 2,080 hours = $31.25/hour.
tools.salary-calculator.faqs.1.question: How do I convert hourly to annual salary?
tools.salary-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Multiply the hourly rate by the hours per week, then by the weeks per year. $20/hour * 40 hours * 52 weeks = $41,600/year.
tools.salary-calculator.faqs.2.question: Are the tax estimates accurate?

tools.savings-calculator.faqs.0.question: How does compound interest affect savings?
tools.savings-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Compound interest accrues on both your principal and accumulated interest. Compounding monthly vs. annually produces slightly higher returns. The difference grows with time and rate.
tools.savings-calculator.faqs.1.question: How do regular deposits affect growth?
tools.savings-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Regular deposits significantly increase the final balance through compounding. Depositing $200/month at a 5% annual return for 10 years = about $31,000 - you contribute $24,000 and interest contributes $7,000.
tools.savings-calculator.faqs.2.question: What's the difference between savings and money market accounts?
tools.savings-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Savings accounts offer a fixed rate and simple access. Money market accounts typically offer higher rates but require higher minimum balances and may offer check-writing privileges. Both are FDIC-insured.
tools.savings-calculator.faqs.3.question: How does inflation affect my savings?
tools.savings-calculator.faqs.3.answer: Inflation erodes purchasing power. 3% inflation reduces purchasing power by 26% over 10 years. Always compare your savings rate to inflation - if the rate is below inflation, your money is losing real value.

tools.tip-calculator.faqs.1.question: Should I tip on the pre-tax or after-tax amount?

tools.url-shortener.faqs.0.answer: Completely free. Short links are created through the public APIs of is.gd and TinyURL, with no account, signup, or payment required.
tools.url-shortener.faqs.1.question: Can I choose a custom short link?
tools.url-shortener.faqs.1.answer: Yes. Enter an alias in the optional custom field and the tool will request that short code from is.gd. Whether the custom code is available depends on the provider's service status and usage limits.
tools.url-shortener.faqs.2.question: Are my links tracked or logged?
tools.url-shortener.faqs.2.answer: No. The tool only forwards your URL to the shortening service and returns the short link. This site performs no statistics, tracking, or storage.
tools.url-shortener.faqs.3.question: Do short links expire?
tools.url-shortener.faqs.3.answer: Links generated by is.gd and TinyURL are permanent and don't expire, unless the target page is removed.
tools.url-shortener.faqs.4.question: Why was my short link generated by TinyURL?
tools.url-shortener.faqs.4.answer: The tool prefers is.gd (which supports structured errors and custom short links). When is.gd is rate-limited or unavailable, it automatically falls back to TinyURL so you still get a working short link.
tools.url-shortener.faqs.5.question: What URLs are supported?
tools.url-shortener.faqs.5.answer: Any public http or https link. Private addresses or localhost will be rejected by the shortening services.
tools.url-shortener.faqs.6.question: Why doesn't my short link open?
tools.url-shortener.faqs.6.answer: Short links are hosted by third-party services is.gd and TinyURL, and these domains may not be accessible from some networks (such as mainland China). The short link itself is valid—if it doesn't open, switch to a network that can reach these domains.

tools.url-slug-generator.faqs.0.question: What is a URL slug?
tools.url-slug-generator.faqs.0.answer: A URL slug is the text portion of a URL that identifies a specific page. It should be readable, SEO-friendly, and contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. For example: "my-blog-post".
tools.url-slug-generator.faqs.1.question: How do I generate a slug?
tools.url-slug-generator.faqs.1.answer: Type or paste text into the input field. The tool automatically converts it into a URL-friendly slug, removing special characters, converting to lowercase, and replacing spaces with hyphens.
tools.url-slug-generator.faqs.2.question: Are slugs important for SEO?
tools.url-slug-generator.faqs.2.answer: Yes. Descriptive slugs help search engines understand page content. They also make it easier for users to predict what a link contains. Good slugs can improve search engine rankings and click-through rates.
tools.url-slug-generator.faqs.3.question: What characters should I use in a slug?
tools.url-slug-generator.faqs.3.answer: Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. Avoid spaces, uppercase, special characters, and consecutive hyphens. Keep slugs short but descriptive.
tools.url-slug-generator.faqs.4.question: Can I customize the slug?
tools.url-slug-generator.faqs.4.answer: Yes. After the initial slug is generated, you can edit it manually for further customization. The tool provides a clean starting point.
tools.url-slug-generator.faqs.5.question: Is the slug generator safe?

tools.url-slug-generator.guide.intro.tit: What is a URL Slug Generator?
tools.url-slug-generator.guide.intro.par: A URL Slug Generator is a free online tool that creates URL-friendly slugs from text. It converts text to lowercase, removes special characters, and replaces spaces with hyphens. All conversion happens in your browser.
Type or paste text into the input field. The tool automatically converts it into a URL-friendly slug. Copy the result for use in URLs.
Keep slugs short but descriptive. Use keywords without stuffing them. Avoid stop words (like a, the, is) unless essential to meaning. Use hyphens to separate words.

tools.401k-calculator.faqs.0.question: How much should I contribute to my 401(k)?
tools.401k-calculator.faqs.0.answer: At minimum, contribute enough to get the full employer match - that's free money. The 2026 contribution limit is $23,500 ($31,000 if 50 or older). Financial advisors often recommend saving 15% of your income for retirement.
tools.401k-calculator.faqs.1.question: What is an employer match?
tools.401k-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Many employers match a percentage of your 401(k) contributions. A common match is 50% of contributions up to 6% of your salary. On a $75,000 salary, that's $2,250 per year in free money.
tools.401k-calculator.faqs.2.question: What return rate should I use?
tools.401k-calculator.faqs.2.answer: The S&P 500 has averaged about 10% per year, or about 7% after inflation. Use 7% for a realistic inflation-adjusted estimate, or 10% for a nominal return estimate. Be conservative when planning.

tools.age-calculator.faqs.0.question: How do I calculate my age?
tools.age-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Age = Current Date - Birth Date. The calculator computes full years, months, and days. For example, born May 15, 1990, and today May 15, 2024 = 34 years old.
tools.age-calculator.faqs.1.question: Why might my age differ in different countries?
tools.age-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Age calculation is universal, but cultural interpretations can differ. Some cultures use nominal age (1 year old at birth), while others use zero age (0 at birth). This calculator uses the international standard.
tools.age-calculator.faqs.2.question: How do I calculate days between two dates?
tools.age-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Days = End Date - Start Date. The calculator accounts for leap years. For example, January 1, 2024 to December 31, 2024 = 365 days (2024 is a leap year).
